successCriteria.description: The AuditRecord entity is exported from the audit module and its action field is typed as the AuditAction enum imported from src/shared/types/index.ts (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT).

The audit service record() method, when called with valid arguments, delegates to repository.create() with a generated UUID id and performedAt set to the current time, and returns the persisted AuditRecord.
The audit service record() method defaults oldValues and newValues to null when those optional arguments are omitted.
The audit service record() method generates a distinct UUID for each invocation (two consecutive calls produce different ids).
The audit service record() method propagates repository errors as rejected promises rather than swallowing them.
The audit repository findByEntity(entityType, entityId) returns audit records ordered chronologically by performedAt (ascending).
The audit repository findByPerformer(performedBy, limit?, offset?) applies optional LIMIT and OFFSET pagination when those parameters are provided.
The audit module barrel (index.ts) re-exports the AuditRecord model, the IAuditRepository interface and AuditRepository class, and the IAuditService interface and AuditService class.

constraints: All database access in the audit module must go through the repository layer (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository); the service must not import the pool or execute SQL directly.
No use of the any type — use unknown with type guards instead (HARNESS.json no-any rule, severity high).
The audit module must import AuditAction from src/shared/types/index.ts rather than redefining the enum locally.
The audit repository must use parameterised queries only — no string-interpolated SQL values (matches the established notification/employee/policy repository pattern and prevents SQL injection).
Other modules may import from the audit module only through its index.ts barrel; no cross-module imports of internal files (AGENTS.md architecture rule 1).
Test files must use the *.test.ts naming convention under tests/ (matching the configured testMatch), not *.spec.ts.
outOfScope: HTTP controller and routes for the audit module — no audit.controller.ts or audit.routes.ts in this phase (controllers and routes are a later phase per PLAN.md).
Zod validation schemas for audit inputs — validation schemas are a later phase per PLAN.md.
The ip_address and user_agent columns present in the audit_logs DB schema are excluded from the AuditRecord entity — the entity matches the phase spec's 10 fields only.
Integration tests against a live PostgreSQL database — this phase includes only Jest unit tests for the audit service with a mocked repository.
Wiring the audit service into the leave module orchestrator — that consumption happens in Phase 7/8 (leave module), not here.

entityInvariants.invariant: An AuditRecord is immutable once persisted — there is no update or delete operation in the repository; the only write path is create().
Every persisted AuditRecord has a non-null performedAt timestamp set by the service at creation time (now); performedAt is never left unset or null.
The action field of an AuditRecord must be one of the AuditAction enum values (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT) defined in src/shared/types/index.ts.

interfaceConstraints.operation: auditService.record(action, entityType, entityId, performedBy, oldValues?, newValues?)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Repository errors (e.g. DB connection failure) propagate as rejected promises; the service does not catch, wrap, or swallow them.
On database failure the promise rejects with the underlying pg error; on success it returns the persisted AuditRecord with DB-populated createdAt/updatedAt.
Returns an empty array when no records match (not null); rejects on database failure.
Returns an empty array when no records match (not null); rejects on database failure. Optional limit/offset are applied only when provided.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The AuditService must follow the NotificationService pattern: constructor-injected repository interface, service generates the UUID via crypto.randomUUID() and sets performedAt to new Date(), then delegates to repository.create() with a CreateAuditRecordInput — the service must not import the pool.

The AuditRepository must follow the NotificationRepository pattern: import pool from ../../shared/db/connection, use parameterised queries, define a private snake_case AuditRow interface, and map rows to camelCase AuditRecord via a mapRowToAuditRecord helper.
The audit barrel index.ts must mirror the notification barrel: re-export the model, the repository interface + class, and the service interface + class.

The AuditRecord.action field and the CreateAuditRecordInput.action field must be typed as the AuditAction enum imported from src/shared/types/index.ts — the enum must not be redefined in the audit module.

The audit service test must mirror the notification service test conventions: jest.Mocked<IAuditRepository> with jest.fn() per method, a makeAuditRecord(overrides) factory, describe('AuditService') → describe('record') → it cases covering create-and-return, null defaults for optional args, unique id per call, and repository error propagation.

integrationPoints.why: The audit module imports the AuditAction enum from shared types; this is the only shared-types dependency for the audit module.
The AuditRepository imports the pg Pool from the shared db connection to execute parameterised queries against the audit_logs table.

The LeaveService orchestrator will consume IAuditService via constructor injection to write audit records on state-changing operations (GP-002); this phase produces the interface that later phases depend on.
